verses.text: In the third year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and surrounded it with his army.

The Lord handed Jehoiakim king of Judah over to him, along with some of the things from the house of God. Nebuchadnezzar took them to the land of Babylonia, to the temple of his god, and put them in the treasure house of his god.
Then the king told Ashpenaz, the chief of his officials, to bring in some young men from Israel, from the royal family and the noble families.

They were to be young men with nothing wrong with their bodies, good-looking, showing wisdom in every subject, well informed, quick to understand, and able to serve in the king's palace. Ashpenaz was to teach them the writings and the language of the Babylonians.
The king gave them a daily share of the rich food he ate and the wine he drank. They were to be trained for three years, and after that they would serve the king.
Among them were some young men from Judah: Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
The chief official gave them new names. He named Daniel Belteshazzar, Hananiah Shadrach, Mishael Meshach, and Azariah Abednego.
But Daniel made up his mind not to make himself unclean with the king's rich food and wine. So he asked the chief official for permission not to make himself unclean.
God caused the chief official to show kindness and sympathy to Daniel.

But the chief official said to Daniel, "I am afraid of my lord the king. He has decided what you should eat and drink. If he sees that you look worse than the other young men your age, he will have my head because of you."
Then Daniel spoke to the guard whom the chief official had put in charge of Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
He said, "Please test us, your servants, for ten days. Give us nothing but vegetables to eat and water to drink.
Then compare how we look with how the young men look who eat the king's rich food. After that, treat us based on what you see."
So the guard agreed to this and tested them for ten days.
At the end of the ten days, they looked healthier and better fed than all the young men who ate the king's rich food.
So the guard took away their rich food and the wine they were supposed to drink, and gave them vegetables instead.
God gave these four young men knowledge and skill in every kind of learning and wisdom. And Daniel could understand visions and dreams of every kind.
At the end of the time the king had set for them to be brought in, the chief official presented them to Nebuchadnezzar.
The king talked with them, and he found no one equal to Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. So they began to serve the king.
Whenever the king asked them about anything that needed wisdom and understanding, he found them ten times better than all the magicians and enchanters in his whole kingdom.
Daniel remained there until the first year of King Cyrus.
